title: Consider using the native `quarto.brand` API instead of hand-parsing `_brand.yml`
description:
`editable.lua` currently finds brand colors by reading and parsing `_brand.yml` directly in `get_brand_palette_colors()`. 
This only sees a literal `_brand.yml`, so it misses brand defined inline under `brand:` in the header, brand from an extension, or light/dark modes.

Consider using the native Quarto Lua API(shipped in **1.7.0**): `quarto.brand.has_mode(mode)` and `quarto.brand.get_color_css(mode, name)`. Since it reads Quarto's *processed* brand data, it covers all those cases and is mode-aware — and it'd drop a good chunk of the YAML-walking code.

One catch: the extension requires `>=1.6.0`, but this API landed in `1.7.0`. So it might mean bumping the requirement.

title: make work without editable classes
description:
Right now you can only modify what is designated to be modified in the source document.

But we could add a button on the UI side, that makes it so the next item to click becomes editable.

This will work because I know how we can find the original element in the source document.

## Initial implementation

Plain `![](image.png)` images have been prototyped on the `main` branch but not yet merged.

## Element support overview

Individual issues track each feasible element type (label: `modify-mode`).

**Prototyped (not yet merged)**

| Element | Capabilities |
|---|---|
| `![](image.png)` | Move, resize, rotate |
| `![](image.png){attrs}` | Move, resize, rotate |
| `![caption](image.png)` | Move, resize, rotate |

**Not feasible**

The following cannot be supported due to fundamental limitations:

- Code chunk figures with 2+ outputs per chunk — ambiguous which figure to target
- Inline equations (`$...$`) — inside text flow, same problem as inline images
- Title slide elements (YAML title/subtitle/author/date) — no slide-body anchor
- Raw HTML blocks (`::: {=html}`) — arbitrary DOM structure
- Background images — slide-level attribute, not a content element
- Other shortcodes (non-arrow) — no predictable DOM structure
- Speaker notes — not visible on slide

## Summary table

| Element | Status | Capabilities | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `![](image.png)` | 🔧 Prototyped | Move, resize, rotate | |
| `![](image.png){attrs}` | 🔧 Prototyped | Move, resize, rotate | |
| `![caption](image.png)` | 🔧 Prototyped | Move, resize, rotate | |
| `![](video.mp4)` | 🟡 Straightforward | Move, resize, rotate | Same mechanism as images |
| Fenced div with class | 🟡 Feasible | Move, resize, rotate, text | Class-based matching within slide chunk |
| Fenced div without class | 🟡 Feasible | Move, resize, rotate, text | Positional matching within slide chunk |
| Callout block | 🟡 Feasible | Move, resize, rotate | Treated as fenced div with `.callout-*` class |
| Columns layout | 🟡 Feasible | Move only | Treated as fenced div; column widths are relative |
| `{.absolute}` without `.editable` | 🟡 Feasible | Move, resize, rotate | Match by existing position attributes |
| Inline image | 🟡 Feasible with care | Move, resize, rotate | Leaves inline flow context on activation |
| Code chunk output div | 🟡 Feasible | Move, resize only | Same chunk matching as figures; no text editing |
| Code chunk figures (named, 1 fig) | 🟡 Very reliable | Move, resize, rotate | Label is literal in source |
| Code chunk figures (unnamed, 1 fig) | 🟡 Feasible | Move, resize, rotate | Positional matching within slide chunk |
| Code chunk figures (any, 2+ figs) | ❌ Ambiguous | — | Can't distinguish figures from same chunk; warning ring |
| Plain paragraph | 🟡 Feasible | Move, resize, rotate, text | Slide chunk + content match; positional fallback |
| Slide title (`##`) | 🟡 Text editing only | Text edit only | Always first line of slide chunk; no move/resize |
| Table | 🟡 Feasible | Move only | Wrap in fenced div; match by first row |
| Arrows (from previous save) | 🟡 Feasible | Move, resize | In-place coordinate update; no wrapping needed |
| Display equation (`$$...$$`) | 🟡 Feasible | Move, resize only | Content match on LaTeX string; wrap in fenced div |
| Inline equation (`$...$`) | ❌ Not practical | — | Inside text flow; same problem as inline images |
| Display code block | 🟡 Feasible | Move, resize only | Anchor by first code line; wrap in fenced div |
| Diagram chunk (`{mermaid}`, `{dot}`) | 🟡 Feasible | Move, resize only | Same chunk matching as figures; SVG output |
| Bullet / ordered list | 🟡 Feasible | Move, resize only | Anchor by first item text; wrap in fenced div |
| Blockquote | 🟡 Feasible | Move, resize only | Anchor by quoted text; wrap in fenced div |
| Observable JS output (`{ojs}`) | 🟡 Feasible | Move, resize only | Same as code chunk output divs |
| Title slide elements | ❌ Not practical | — | YAML-generated; no slide-body anchor |
| Raw HTML blocks | ❌ Arbitrary HTML | — | No predictable structure or anchor |
| Background images | ❌ Different mechanism | — | Slide-level attribute, not a content element |
| Other shortcodes | ❌ Arbitrary HTML | — | No predictable DOM structure or source anchor |
| Speaker notes | ❌ Not applicable | — | Not visible |

title: modify mode: use `{{< contents >}}` shortcode to position code and output independently
description:
Follow-up to #113 / #112. See parent #48 and related items #114 (diagrams) and #115 (equations) which face the same source-vs-output coupling.

Quarto 1.6+ provides the [`{{< contents >}}` shortcode](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/contents.html), which takes the contents of a labeled cell (or any `id`-bearing div/span) and renders it at the shortcode's location.

## The problem this solves

Today, modify mode for code chunk outputs (#113) wraps the entire chunk fence in `::: {.absolute …}` — source code and output move together as a single block. When `echo: true`, you can't position the visible source separately from its output. For figure chunks (#112), the same wrapping moves the literal code fence but anchors the figure to the chunk's source location, not where the user dragged it.

## Proposed approach

Instead of (or in addition to) wrapping the chunk fence in `::: {.absolute …}`, activation in modify mode could:

1. Ensure the chunk has a label (use `#| label:` if present, otherwise synthesize one like `auto-cell-N`).
2. Leave the source chunk in place at its natural document position (it becomes the "definition").
3. Insert a positioned reference at the dragged location:
   ```
   ::: {.absolute left=…px top=…px width=…px height=…px}
   {{< contents the-label >}}
   :::
   ```

## What this unlocks

- **Independent placement** of code and output: with `echo: true`, the user could activate the cell, choose "show source here" vs "show output here" via the toolbar, and serialize each as a separate `{{< contents … >}}` reference (the source side may need a label on the source `<pre>` rather than the cell — TBD).
- **Multiple views** of the same output (e.g. a small inset and a large detail) without re-running the chunk.
- **Cleaner round-trip**: source chunks stay readable in the `.qmd` (no `::: {.absolute …}` wrapping the chunk fence); positioning is purely additive via `{{< contents >}}`.
- **Figure chunks** (#112): the figure becomes a `{{< contents >}}` reference at the dragged position, regardless of where the chunk lives in source — solves the anchor problem cleanly.

## Open questions

- Auto-labeling: synthesize a stable label when none exists, or require the user to name the chunk before activation?
- Splitting source from output: contents pulls the whole cell — for echo=true, we may need to render source as a non-executed `\`\`\`python` block separately and reference only the output. Possibly easier than it sounds since Quarto produces predictable element ids for cell-output divs.
- Interaction with existing serializer: the current "wrap chunk" path stays valid for the common case (echo=false, one output); contents-based positioning could be opt-in, perhaps via a toolbar toggle when the cell is activated.
- Quarto version gate: contents requires Quarto 1.6+ — need to detect or document.

## Related

- #113 (code chunk output divs / OJS — current implementation that this would extend)
- #112 (single-figure code chunks — strongest candidate to benefit)
- #48 (parent: make modify mode work without `.editable`)
- #114 (mermaid/dot diagram chunks — same shape as figures)

title: if you click to modify an element, but then don't actually do anything we should not do anything
description: this would help reduce unused .absolute divs

title: modify mode: re-activation of already-positioned elements (general)
description:
Several modify-mode classifiers explicitly skip elements that are already wrapped in `::: {.absolute …}` (or carry `{.absolute}` themselves). That means once an element has been positioned and saved, it can no longer be moved through modify mode — the only path to update its position is to hand-edit the QMD.

This has already been solved one-element-type-at-a-time for **images** (#122) and **plain `.absolute` divs** (#119). The same gap exists for every other element type added since:

- paragraphs, bullet lists, ordered lists, blockquotes (#109, #110)
- display code blocks (#111)
- code chunk outputs (#113)
- tables — pipe / grid / HTML / list / captioned (#117)
- positioned arrows already round-trip in place (#118)

For tables specifically, see [this comment](https://github.com/EmilHvitfeldt/quarto-revealjs-editable/pull/SOON) — saving a table wraps it in `::: {.absolute …}`, and on next render the table is no longer activatable.

### Current behavior

Each classifier filters its DOM candidates with some variant of:

```js
if (el.classList.contains('absolute')) continue;
if (el.closest('div.absolute')) continue;
```

so an element inside a previously-saved positioning wrapper is invisible to modify mode. The fenced-divs classifier *does* match the outer `::: {.absolute}` wrapper, but it activates the wrapper as a generic positioned div — not as the element type inside (no table controls for a `.absolute`-wrapped table, no Quill for a `.absolute`-wrapped paragraph, etc.).

### Goal

Tackle this once, consistently, for **all** modify-mode element types. A previously-saved element should be re-activatable through modify mode and behave like it did the first time it was activated:

- pick the right capabilities (move-only for tables/lists/code, move+resize+rotate for text/images, etc.)
- preserve the source anchor so save writes back to the same block (in-place rewrite of the existing `.absolute` attrs, not a second wrap)
- not double-wrap; not lose attributes the user added by hand to the existing fence

### Sketch of an approach

Rather than each classifier rolling its own check, introduce a small shared pass that:

1. Walks the slide for `div.absolute` wrappers (and bare elements with `.absolute`).
2. Looks inside to identify what's wrapped (table, paragraph, list, code block, callout, etc.).
3. Routes activation to the existing per-type setup, but with an \"already-positioned\" flag so the serializer rewrites the existing fence line in place (the same path the `.absolute` div classifier already uses).

The `_input_file` source anchor for the existing `.absolute` fence is already parseable — `parseFencedDivOpens` finds them, and `getFencedDivIdentifier` could be extended (or paired with a content sniffer) to report what kind of element is inside.

### Acceptance

- An `.absolute`-wrapped instance of every element type listed above is classified valid in modify mode.
- Clicking it re-activates with the right capabilities for that type.
- Saving rewrites the existing `.absolute` fence in place — no nested wrappers, no lost attrs.
- E2E coverage for at least one already-positioned instance of each type.

Closes the pattern that issues #119 and #122 opened. Probably worth doing as a shared utility + one PR per element type, rather than rewriting every classifier in one go.

title: modify mode: code chunk figures (single-figure chunks)
description:
Part of #48.

Code chunk figures can be targeted when the chunk produces exactly one figure, detected at runtime by checking that no sibling image shares the same chunk prefix in the filename (e.g. `named-single-1.png` is unique; `named-multi-1.png` and `named-multi-2.png` share a prefix and are excluded with a warning ring).

**Named chunks** (e.g. ` ```{r my-plot}`) are the strongest case — the label appears literally in the QMD source, so the chunk is findable without positional matching.

**Unnamed chunks** require positional matching: Nth unnamed chunk in DOM = Nth unnamed chunk in source chunk.

**Capabilities:** move, resize, rotate

**Write-back:** wrap the source chunk in a positioned fenced div

```markdown
```{r}            →      ::: {.absolute left=100px top=200px}
plot(x)                  ```{r}
```                      plot(x)
                         ```
                         :::
```

Multi-figure chunks (2+ outputs) show an amber warning ring and are not clickable.

title: modify mode: display equations ($$...$$)
description:
Part of #48.

Block equations (`$$E = mc^2$$`) render as their own container element (MathJax/KaTeX wrapper). Moving and resizing a display equation is a real use case. Text editing via Quill is not appropriate — the content is raw LaTeX.

**Capabilities:** move, resize only

**Source anchor:** the LaTeX string itself, matched within the slide chunk between `$$` delimiters. The same equation appearing twice on the same slide is very unlikely.

**Write-back:** wrap the `$$...$$` block in a positioned fenced div

```markdown
$$E = mc^2$$   →   ::: {.absolute left=100px top=200px}
                   $$E = mc^2$$
                   :::
```

**Note:** the DOM target should be the outer container element, not the rendered SVG/HTML produced by MathJax or KaTeX.

title: un-absolute items
description: right now anytime to modify something it becomes absolute. there should be a way to remove the absolute styling to have it snap back

title: modify mode: diagram chunks ({mermaid}, {dot})
description:
Part of #48. Mermaid and Graphviz diagram chunks produce SVG output rendered into a `
` rather than a raster ``. The chunk-matching logic is identical to code chunk figures — named chunks by label, unnamed by positional index. Diagrams almost always produce one output per chunk so multi-output ambiguity is rarely an issue. **Capabilities:** move, resize only **Source anchor:** named chunks by label; unnamed chunks by positional index within slide chunk **Write-back:** wrap the source chunk in a positioned fenced div

title: modify mode: tables (move only)
description:
Part of #48.

Tables can be moved as a unit. Resizing is not meaningful — table width is determined by content and column definitions, not a CSS width on a wrapper.

**Capabilities:** move only

**Source anchor:** first row (header line) of the table within the slide chunk; positional fallback for duplicate headers

**Write-back:** wrap the entire table block in a positioned fenced div

```markdown
| A | B |          →    ::: {.absolute left=100px top=200px}
|---|---|               | A | B |
| 1 | 2 |               |---|---|
                        | 1 | 2 |
                        :::
```

title: Add delete functionality for dynamically added elements
description:
## Summary

Currently, there is no way to delete elements that have been dynamically added via the toolbar (text boxes, slides, arrows). Once an element is created, it can only be modified but not removed.

## Affected Elements

- **Text boxes** - Added via Add → Text
- **Slides** - Added via Add → Slide  
- **Arrows** - Added via Add → Arrow

## Expected Behavior

Users should be able to delete dynamically added elements through one or more of the following methods:

1. **Keyboard shortcut** - Press `Delete` or `Backspace` key when element is selected
2. **Context menu** - Right-click on element to show delete option
3. **Toolbar button** - Add a delete button that appears when an element is selected
4. **Delete handle** - Add a small × button on selected elements

## Implementation Considerations

- Only newly added elements (`.editable-new`) should be deletable - original document elements should not be removable
- Deletion should remove the element from:
  - The DOM
  - The `NewElementRegistry` tracking arrays (`newDivs`, `newSlides`, `newArrows`)
- Consider adding undo support for accidental deletions
- For slides: deleting a slide should also delete any elements added to that slide

## Related

This was identified during arrow feature testing as a gap in functionality.

title: modify mode: code chunk output divs and Observable JS
description:
Part of #48.

Code chunks that produce non-image output (HTML tables, printed output, interactive widgets) render as `<div class="cell-output-display">` elements. Observable JS (`{ojs}`) chunks produce the same structure. Both are moveable and resizable but must not be text-editable — the content is generated output, not user-written prose.

**Capabilities:** move, resize only — `fontControls` and `editText` must be excluded even though the element is a `<div>`

**Source anchor:** named chunks by label; unnamed chunks by positional index within slide chunk

**Write-back:** wrap the source chunk in a positioned fenced div

title: modify mode: display code blocks
description:
Part of #48.

Non-executed fenced code blocks (e.g. ` ```python `) render as `<pre><code>` elements. Moving them on a slide is a real use case; text editing is not appropriate (raw code, not prose).

**Capabilities:** move, resize only

**Source anchor:** first line of code content within slide chunk

**Write-back:** wrap the fenced code block in a positioned fenced div

```markdown
```python          →    ::: {.absolute left=100px top=200px}
x = 1                   ```python
```                      x = 1

title: modify mode: arrows from previous save
description:
Part of #48.

Arrows added via **Add → Arrow** in the current session are already fully editable. This issue covers arrows that exist in the source from a previous save but are not registered in the current session — they are currently invisible to modify mode.

Arrow shortcodes appear literally in the QMD source with coordinates already embedded:

```markdown
{{< arrow from="100,200" to="400,300" position="absolute" >}}
```

Since arrows already carry `position="absolute"`, write-back is an in-place update of coordinate values — no fenced div wrapping needed.

**Capabilities:** move, resize

**Source anchor:** `from=` and `to=` coordinate values within the slide chunk (same coordinates appearing twice on the same slide is extremely unlikely)

**Write-back:** in-place coordinate update in the shortcode

title: modify mode: inline images (inside paragraphs)
description:
Part of #48. Images embedded inside a paragraph (`some text ![](img.png) more text`) render as `` inside a `

`. The src is still findable in the QMD source, so the same src-lookup approach as plain images works. **Capabilities:** move, resize, rotate **Source anchor:** literal src within the slide chunk **Write-back:** same regex as plain images, replacing `](src)` — must be careful not to match fenced div form **Caveat:** activating an inline image pulls it out of the text flow and makes it absolutely positioned, which will visually displace the surrounding paragraph text. This is a user expectation issue to communicate clearly in the UI.

title: Modify panel shows green type pills for all classifiers, not just those present on the slide
description:
## Bug

When the user clicks the **Modify** button, the toolbar panel shows a row of green pills (e.g. \"Images\", \"Videos\", \"Positioned divs\", \"Slide titles\") for every registered \`ModifyModeClassifier\`, even if none of those element types exist on the current slide.

## Reproduction

1. Open any presentation with the extension active.
2. Click the **Modify** toolbar button.
3. The panel displays green type pills for all classifier labels unconditionally.

## Root cause

\`buildModifyPanel()\` in \`src/modify-mode.js\` calls \`ModifyModeClassifier.getLabels()\` to populate the list — this returns **all** registered labels regardless of what \`applyClassification()\` actually found on the slide. The two calls are independent, so the pill list is never filtered by what is actually present.

## Expected behaviour

The green type pills should only appear for element types that have at least one **valid** (clickable) element on the current slide. If no valid elements exist for a classifier, its pill should be omitted (or the panel should show a \"nothing to edit here\" message).

## Suggested fix

Pass the classification results from \`applyClassification()\` into \`buildModifyPanel()\` (or re-run classification before building the panel) and filter the label list to only classifiers that returned at least one valid element.

title: modify mode: bullet lists, ordered lists, and blockquotes
description:
Part of #48.

These block-level text containers can all be moved as a unit using the same slide-scoped approach as paragraphs.

- **Bullet lists** (`- item`) → `<ul>`
- **Ordered lists** (`1. item`) → `<ol>`
- **Blockquotes** (`> text`) → `<blockquote>`

**Capabilities:** move, resize only — text editing not included (list/quote structure does not round-trip cleanly through Quill)

**Source anchor:** first item/line text content within slide chunk; positional fallback for duplicates

**Write-back:** wrap the entire block in a positioned fenced div

title: modify mode: plain paragraphs
description:
Part of #48.

Plain paragraph text can be made moveable using slide-scoped matching. Two strategies in order:

1. **Content match** — search the slide chunk for the paragraph text (reliable when unique on the slide)
2. **Positional fallback** — Nth paragraph in DOM = Nth paragraph in source chunk

**Capabilities:** move, resize, rotate, text edit

**Source anchor:** text content within slide chunk

**Write-back:** wrap paragraph in a positioned fenced div

```markdown
Some paragraph text    →    ::: {.absolute left=100px top=200px}
                            Some paragraph text
                            :::
```

**Note:** matching must be done against the raw QMD source, not the DOM `textContent`, to avoid mismatches from inline markdown (`**bold**`, `*italic*`).

title: modify mode: fenced divs (with class, without class, callouts, columns)
description:
Part of #48.

Fenced divs are the most general text container in Quarto and cover several element types:

- **With a distinctive class** (`::: {.my-class}`) — class name is the anchor; reliable
- **Without a class** (`:::`) — positional index within slide chunk
- **Callout blocks** (`::: {.callout-note}`) — same as fenced div with `.callout-*` class
- **Columns layout** (`::: {.columns}`) — move as unit; resize less meaningful since column widths are relative

**Capabilities:** move, resize, rotate, text edit (except columns: move only)

**Source anchor:** class name within slide chunk; positional fallback for classless divs

**Write-back:** add `{.absolute ...}` attributes to the opening `:::` fence line

title: modify mode: slide title text editing (## heading)
description:
Part of #48.

Slide titles cannot be moved or resized — Reveal.js uses the `<h2>` structurally for navigation and internal links. However, text editing is feasible. The title is always the first `## ` line of the slide chunk, so there is no ambiguity in locating it.

**Capabilities:** text edit only — no move or resize

**Source anchor:** always the first `## ` line of the slide chunk

**Write-back:** replace the heading text in place

```markdown
## My Slide   →   ## My Updated Slide
```

**Notes:**
- Basic inline formatting (bold, italic) serializes back into the `##` line
- Font size, color, and alignment require a span: `## [My Slide]{style="color: red"}` — heading-level attributes apply to the slide container, not the text

title: modify mode: video support (![](video.mp4))
description:
Part of #48.

Videos inserted with `![](video.mp4)` render as `<video>` tags with a src that matches the QMD path. The same src-lookup and regex approach used for plain images applies directly — this should be straightforward to add.

**Capabilities:** move, resize, rotate

**Source anchor:** literal src in QMD source

**Write-back:** same as images — replace `](src)` with `](src){.absolute ...}`

title: modify mode: {.absolute} images without {.editable}
description: Part of #48. Images previously saved with `{.absolute}` attributes (but without `{.editable}`) are not currently activatable in modify mode. For example, after a round-trip save of: \`\`\` ![](image.png){.editable} \`\`\` the QMD becomes: \`\`\` ![](image.png){.absolute left=100px top=80px width=200px height=120px} \`\`\` On the next render this produces `` in the DOM. Neither the existing image classifier (which skips `img.absolute` to avoid conflict with #119) nor the `div.absolute` classifier (which only queries `div.absolute`) picks it up. ## Proposed approach Follow the same pattern as #119: - **Detect:** `slideEl.querySelectorAll("img.absolute")` — skip if already in `editableRegistry` - **Match to source:** read `left`/`top`/`width`/`height` from inline styles; verify against the slide's QMD chunk using a lookahead regex on `](src){.absolute ...}` - **Activate:** capture original position, clear `el.style.left`/`el.style.top`, call `setupImageWhenReady`, then fix container position via `waitForRegistryThenFixPosition` - **Serialize:** replace `](src){.absolute ...}` block in the correct slide chunk using the original position values as the matching key The helpers added in #119 (`getAbsolutePosition`, `makeAbsoluteBlockRegex`, `waitForRegistryThenFixPosition`) are directly reusable. The main difference from #119 is the QMD source pattern (`](src){...}` instead of a fenced div) and using the image src as an additional matching key alongside the position values. ## Capabilities Move, resize, rotate — same as a fully `{.editable}` image.

title: modify mode: {.absolute} elements without {.editable}
description:
Part of #48.

Elements saved with `{.absolute}` attributes from a previous session but without `{.editable}` are currently invisible to modify mode. These could be re-activated by detecting `position: absolute` in the rendered DOM and matching them in the source by their existing position attributes.

**Capabilities:** move, resize, rotate (same as any fully editable element)

**Source anchor:** existing position attribute values (`left=`, `top=`, `width=`, `height=`) are unique enough to identify the right line within the slide chunk

**Write-back:** update the existing `{.absolute ...}` attribute block in place — no wrapping needed

title: Add defensive null checks for global variables
Add image editing context panel to top bar
description:
## Summary

When an image element is selected, the top bar should switch from the default panel to an image-specific context panel (similar to how the arrow panel works today).

## Motivation

The top bar redesign (#100) introduced a two-zone layout with swappable right-zone panels. The arrow panel is already implemented. Images should get the same treatment — selecting an image replaces the default add/modify buttons with image-specific controls.

## Proposed Controls

The image context panel (`.toolbar-panel-image`) should expose controls relevant to the selected image:

- **Opacity** — slider or numeric input
- **Border radius** — rounded corners control
- **Object fit** — cover / contain / fill toggle
- **Crop** — integrate with or complement the cropping work in #78
- **Replace image** — open file picker to swap the source
- **Flip** — horizontal / vertical flip toggles
- **Reset** — revert to original dimensions/position

Exact set of controls can be refined as the feature is implemented.

## Implementation Notes

- Follow the same pattern as `createArrowStyleControls()` in `src/arrows.js`
- Call `showRightPanel('image')` on image element selection, `showRightPanel('default')` on deselection
- Add `.toolbar-panel-image` to `createFloatingToolbar()` in `src/toolbar.js`
- Serialization of new properties via `PropertySerializers` in `src/registries.js`

## Related Issues

- #100 — Top bar toolbar (parent feature)
- #78 — Image cropping (crop control should integrate here)
- #75 — Add images (images are the elements this panel targets)
- #101 — Text editor context panel (sibling panel, same architecture)

title: Move text editor (Quill) toolbar into top bar as context panel
description:
## Summary

Currently the Quill rich-text toolbar floats above the selected text element. It should move into the top bar as a **context panel** — replacing the Add/Modify panel when a text element is selected, consistent with how arrow controls work in #100.

## Motivation

- The floating Quill toolbar is visually disconnected from the rest of the editing UI
- The top bar already has a panel-switching architecture (default → arrow → …) that makes adding a text panel a natural extension
- Keeps all editing controls in one predictable location

## Design

When a `div.editable` element is selected/enters edit mode, the right zone of the top bar should switch to a **text panel** containing the Quill formatting controls (bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, color, size, alignment, etc.).

When the element is deselected / edit mode exits, the right zone returns to the default panel (Add + Modify).

```
nothing selected:  [ Add ▾ ] [ Modify ]
text selected:     [ B ] [ I ] [ U ] [ S ] | [ color ] [ size ] | [ ⇤ ] [ ⇔ ] [ ⇥ ]
```

## Technical notes

- The Quill toolbar is currently positioned absolutely above the element (`bottom: 100%`) and shown/hidden via `.editing` class
- Wiring Quill formatting commands to top-bar buttons requires keeping a reference to the active Quill instance
- The existing `editMode` control on the element can stay (or become a toggle that activates the text panel)
- Add a `.toolbar-panel-text` container in `createFloatingToolbar()` alongside the existing arrow panel

## Related

- #100 — top bar implementation (panel-switching architecture lives here)
- #38 — text formatting features that belong in this panel
- #48 — Modify button (click-to-edit) will likely activate this panel

title: Arrow support: Waypoints and smooth curves
description:
## Summary

Add support for complex multi-point arrow paths with waypoints and smooth curve interpolation.

## Features to implement

- `waypoints` - Multiple intermediate points for complex paths (e.g., "200,150 300,200 400,150")
- `smooth` - Smooth curves through waypoints using Catmull-Rom or similar spline interpolation

## Example usage

```markdown
{{< arrow from="100,200" to="500,200" waypoints="200,100 300,300 400,100" smooth="true" >}}
```

## Considerations

- Waypoints create a polyline path through specified points
- With `smooth="true"`, generate smooth curves through all points (not just Bezier with 2 control points)
- Each waypoint should have a draggable handle in edit mode
- Need UI for adding/removing waypoints (maybe click on line to add, right-click to remove)
- Serialization format needs to support variable number of points

## UI Implementation

- Show waypoint handles (different color from start/end)
- Double-click on arrow line to add a new waypoint at that position
- Delete key or context menu to remove selected waypoint
- Waypoints should be draggable like other handles
- Style panel could show waypoint count and smooth toggle

## Complexity

This is a more advanced feature that significantly extends the current arrow model. Consider:
- Start with basic waypoint support (polyline)
- Add smooth interpolation as enhancement
- May need to refactor arrow data model to support variable points

title: Arrow support: Extend undo/redo to arrow operations
description:
## Problem

Arrow creation, movement, and styling changes are not integrated with the undo/redo system. The existing undo system (\`pushUndoState()\`, \`undoStack\`, etc.) only tracks editable elements in \`editableRegistry\`.

## Impact

Users cannot undo arrow changes with Ctrl+Z. This includes:
- Creating an arrow
- Moving arrow endpoints
- Changing arrow styles (color, width, dash, etc.)
- Toggling curve mode
- Moving control points

## Proposed Solution

Extend the undo system to track arrow state:

### Option A: Extend existing system
Add arrows to the state snapshots captured by \`pushUndoState()\`:
- Include \`NewElementRegistry.newArrows\` in state
- Capture arrow data objects (positions, styles)
- Restore on undo/redo

### Option B: Separate arrow undo stack
Create a parallel undo system for arrows:
- Simpler to implement
- Avoids mixing concerns
- But Ctrl+Z would need to decide which stack to pop

### Considerations
- Arrow data is stored in memory (not DOM attributes like editables)
- Need to deep-clone arrow objects for snapshots
- Control point positions need restoration

## Related

- #26 (closed) - Added undo/redo for element positioning

## Priority

Low - Feature enhancement, complex implementation

title: Review innerHTML usage for security
description: ## Summary Several places use `innerHTML` which could be XSS vectors if content is untrusted. ## Locations ### 1. User content serialization (serialization.js:96) ```javascript let text = quillEditor ? quillEditor.innerHTML.trim() : element.innerHTML.trim(); ``` This reads user-edited content. While it's being serialized to QMD (not rendered), the content could contain malicious scripts that get saved to the file. **Risk:** Low - Content is written to a .qmd file, not executed. However, if the QMD is later rendered without sanitization, it could be a vector. ### 2. Quill toolbar creation (quill.js:72-82) ```javascript toolbarContainer.innerHTML = \` ... \`; ``` **Risk:** None - This is static trusted content. ### 3. Toolbar button creation (registries.js:243) ```javascript btn.innerHTML = \`\${config.icon}...\`; ``` **Risk:** Low - Icons come from internal config, not user input. ## Recommendations 1. **For user content (serialization.js):** Consider sanitizing HTML before processing, or document that users are responsible for their own content security. 2. **For static UI:** Add comments marking these as trusted: ```javascript // TRUSTED: Static UI content, not user-controlled toolbarContainer.innerHTML = \`...\`; ``` 3. **Consider DOMPurify:** For any case where user content might be rendered: ```javascript import DOMPurify from 'dompurify'; const clean = DOMPurify.sanitize(userContent); ``` ## Priority Low - The actual XSS risk is minimal since content goes to files, not direct rendering. But worth documenting the decision.

title: Docs: Add JSDoc comments and slim down ARCHITECTURE.md
description:
## Summary

Move implementation details from ARCHITECTURE.md into JSDoc comments in the code, keeping ARCHITECTURE.md focused on high-level concepts.

Related to #67 - this pairs well with the module split.

## Current State

ARCHITECTURE.md contains both:
- High-level concepts (how systems interact, data flow)
- Implementation details (function signatures, state object properties)

## Proposed Changes

### Add JSDoc to code

```javascript
/**
 * Wraps a DOM element with editable capabilities.
 * Manages state synchronization between internal state and DOM.
 */
class EditableElement {
  /**
   * @param {HTMLElement} element - The DOM element to wrap
   * @param {Object} options - Configuration options
   * @param {string[]} options.capabilities - List of capability names to enable
   */
  constructor(element, options) { ... }

  /**
   * Applies internal state to the DOM element.
   * Called after state changes to update visual representation.
   */
  syncToDOM() { ... }
}

/**
 * Registry for element control buttons (font size, alignment, etc).
 * Controls are shown when an element is selected.
 * @example
 * ControlRegistry.register("myControl", {
 *   icon: "🔧",
 *   appliesTo: ["div"],
 *   onClick: (element) => { ... }
 * });
 */
const ControlRegistry = { ... };
```

### Slim down ARCHITECTURE.md

Keep only:
- System overview and data flow diagrams
- How registries/capabilities/modules interact
- Design decisions and rationale
- Extension points for contributors

Remove:
- Detailed function signatures (now in JSDoc)
- State object property lists (now in class docs)
- Serializer details (now in module docs)

## Benefits

- Docs stay in sync with code
- AI agents see context when reading functions
- IDE support (tooltips, autocomplete)
- ARCHITECTURE.md becomes a focused onboarding doc
- Pairs well with module split (#67)

title: Refactor: Split editable.js into multiple modules
description:
## Summary

`editable.js` is currently ~3850 lines in a single file. Splitting it into logical modules would improve maintainability and make it easier for AI agents to work with the codebase.

## Proposed Module Structure

```
_extensions/editable/
├── src/
│   ├── registries.js      # ControlRegistry, ToolbarRegistry, NewElementRegistry
│   ├── capabilities.js    # move, resize, rotate, fontControls capabilities
│   ├── editable-element.js # EditableElement class, state management
│   ├── arrows.js          # Arrow system (creation, styling, serialization)
│   ├── colors.js          # Color system, brand colors, palette
│   ├── serialization.js   # PropertySerializers, QMD generation
│   ├── toolbar.js         # Floating toolbar UI
│   ├── undo.js            # Undo/redo system
│   └── main.js            # Initialization, entry point
├── editable.js            # Bundled output (generated)
├── editable.css
└── editable.lua
```

## Benefits

- **Targeted code reads** - Work with 200-400 line files instead of 3800+
- **Cleaner edits** - Reduced risk of unintended changes to unrelated code
- **Better parallelization** - Multiple agents/developers can work on different modules
- **Clearer architecture** - Module boundaries make structure explicit
- **Easier testing** - Could unit test modules independently

## Implementation

1. Add a build step using esbuild (fast, zero-config)
2. Split code into modules with ES imports/exports
3. Bundle to single `editable.js` for Quarto
4. Update package.json with build scripts
5. Update CONTRIBUTING.md with build instructions

## Build Script Example

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "build": "esbuild src/main.js --bundle --outfile=editable.js --format=iife"
  }
}
```

## Considerations

- Quarto extensions expect a single JS file, so bundling is required
- Need to ensure source maps work for debugging
- May want to add a watch mode for development

Arrow support: Curve parallel offset not geometrically correct
description:
## Known Limitation

The `updateArrowLineStyle()` function uses CSS transform to offset parallel lines for double/triple line styles:

```javascript
extraPath.setAttribute("transform", \`translate(0, \${offsetAmount})\`);
```

**Location:** `editable.js` lines 1893-1962

## Impact

For curved arrows, this creates a **vertical** offset rather than a **perpendicular** offset to the curve. The parallel lines don't follow the curve correctly - they're shifted up/down uniformly.

![Diagram showing issue]
- Straight arrows: parallel lines appear correct
- Curved arrows: parallel lines diverge/converge incorrectly

## Note

This matches the Lua implementation, so behavior is consistent between the editor and rendered output.

## Potential Fix

For proper parallel curves, would need to calculate offset paths perpendicular to the curve at each point. This involves:
- Calculating tangent vectors along the curve
- Computing perpendicular offsets at each sample point
- Building a new path from offset points

This is mathematically complex (especially for Bezier curves) and may not be worth the effort for an edge case feature.

## Priority

Low - Edge case, complex fix, consistent with Lua behavior

title: Fix failing 'New Elements in Save Flow' tests
description:
## Summary

8 tests in `toolbar.spec.js` are failing related to saving new elements (slides, text) in the correct order.

## Failing Tests

**New Elements in Save Flow (7):**
1. Text on original slide after adding new slides
2. New slides at different original positions
3. Mixed: new slides at multiple positions with text on each
4. Original element modifications alongside new elements
5. New slide after the last original slide
6. New slide with no content saves correctly
7. Interleaved operations save correctly

**Edge Cases - Insertion order (1):**
8. Alternating: add slide -> add text -> add slide -> add text pattern

## Issue

All failures show position assertion errors - the saved content has elements in unexpected positions. For example:

```
expect(groupAPos).toBeGreaterThan(slide1Pos);
Expected: > 124
Received: 107
```

The tests expect new elements to be inserted at specific positions relative to original slides, but the actual saved output has them in different positions.

## Root Cause

Likely an issue with `NewElementRegistry` tracking or the save serialization logic when handling:
- Multiple new slides at different positions
- Text elements on new vs original slides
- Interleaved add operations

## To Reproduce

```bash
cd testing
npx playwright test e2e/toolbar.spec.js --grep "New Elements in Save Flow"
```

Add undo/redo support for element positioning
description:
## Problem

When users make positioning or sizing mistakes while editing elements, there's no way to undo. They must manually reposition/resize or reload the page and start over.

## Proposed Solution

Add undo/redo functionality with:
- **Ctrl+Z** to undo last action
- **Ctrl+Y** (or Ctrl+Shift+Z) to redo

### What would be tracked

| State | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Position | Container left/top after drag |
| Dimensions | Element width/height after resize |
| Font size | After A-/A+ button clicks |
| Text alignment | After alignment button clicks |

### Implementation approach

1. Create global undo/redo stacks (arrays of state snapshots)
2. Capture state at the **start** of drag/resize operations
3. Push to undo stack when action **completes**
4. Clear redo stack on new actions
5. Limit stack size (e.g., 50 entries) to prevent memory issues
6. Debounce continuous actions to capture only start/end states

### Considerations

- **ContentEditable**: Text editing has browser-native undo - may want to let that handle itself
- **Granularity**: Per-element vs global snapshots (global is simpler)
- **Memory**: Many rapid drags could fill stack - debouncing helps
- **UI**: Optional undo/redo buttons in menu (keyboard shortcuts are primary)

### Estimated complexity

~100-150 lines of JavaScript

## Alternatives considered

- Browser-level undo: Only works for text, not positioning
- Reset button: Less useful than granular undo
- Auto-save snapshots: More complex, less intuitive

title: "Save Edits" fails in quarto project
description:
Hi, first of all thank you for creating this extension, I've been wanting something like this for ages to help me move and resize images instead of guessing at the pixel values!

# Bug description

Pressing "Save Edits" inside a quarto project fails to save the updated .qmd file to disk. On opening the browser console, I see a failed GET request for `http://localhost:5926/example.qmd`, with `404 Not Found`, followed by 
```
Error reading index.qmd: Error: HTTP error! status: 404
    readIndexQmd http://localhost:5926/site_libs/revealjs/plugin/revealeditable/editable.js:404
    saveMovedElts http://localhost:5926/site_libs/revealjs/plugin/revealeditable/editable.js:392
    onclick http://localhost:5926/example.html#/text:1
[editable.js:409:13](http://localhost:5926/site_libs/revealjs/plugin/revealeditable/editable.js)
    readIndexQmd http://localhost:5926/site_libs/revealjs/plugin/revealeditable/editable.js:409
    saveMovedElts http://localhost:5926/site_libs/revealjs/plugin/revealeditable/editable.js:392
    onclick http://localhost:5926/example.html#/text:1
Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: can't access property "replace", text is null
    replaceeditableOccurrences http://localhost:5926/site_libs/revealjs/plugin/revealeditable/editable.js:459
    saveMovedElts http://localhost:5926/site_libs/revealjs/plugin/revealeditable/editable.js:395
    onclick http://localhost:5926/example.html#/text:1
```

The extension works like a charm when `example.qmd` is previewed outside a project context. The file downloads successfully and I can also navigate to it in the browser at `http://localhost:5926/example.qmd`. 

However, inside a project context, the same URL says "Not Found" so the extension can't download it either.

Furthermore, if I remove `example.qmd` from the project render target, by editing `_quarto.yml` to only render the other pages:

```
project:
  type: website
  render:
    - index.qmd
    - about.qmd
```
Then when I preview the website I can navigate to the raw `example.qmd` file from the index. Then, I add `example.qmd` to the render target again and I can download it with the "Save Edits" button as expected.

It seems that `http://localhost:5926/example.qmd` is empty when a project is first previewed, but this is fixed if the `example.qmd` file is removed from the render target and then re-added, forcing quarto to make the source markdown available at the address. In other words, `example.qmd` gets copied to the `_site` folder of the project alongside `example.html` when `example.qmd` is removed from the render target. I don't know if this is expected quarto behavior.

# Steps to reproduce

1. Initialize a quarto project of type website:
```
quarto create project website editable --no-prompt
cd editable
```
2. Put `example.qmd` in the project folder. 
3. Link to it from `index.qmd`:
````qmd
---
title: "editable"
---

Try editing [this page](./example.qmd).
````

4. Install the plugin:
`
quarto add emilhvitfeldt/quarto-revealjs-editable
`

5. Render the website:
`
quarto preview
`

6. Navigate to the editable slides and click on "Save Edits" from the tools menu. Nothing happens because `example.qmd` is not initially available at the same address as when rendering individual files outside a project.
